name: Week 31 Optional KB — Bent Press Flow + Figure-8 Complex
description:
**Optional — take it whenever a window opens.** The three gym days complete the week; this is a bonus, not a debt.

**The Bent Press Flow stays as the anchor.** **The figure-8 complex comes back after a long absence** — the bell passes between the legs in a figure-eight, and the hand that catches it behind the leg keeps going straight into a clean to the rack. The pass *is* the clean entry, which is the whole skill.

**Nothing in the figure-8 goes overhead**, which matters this week: a new crackle showed up in the left shoulder on pull day. Keep the bell light and unhurried. One round of each is a complete session on a bad-sleep day.

dayOverview.theme: One overhead skill flow, one hand-switching complex that never leaves the rack, and a short strength round between them. Written short and optional: two rounds of each when fresh, one when the night was bad, and either version counts as done.

spotlights.why: It has been away for months and it is the best hand-eye drill in the library. The catch happens under load behind the leg and flows straight into the rack — there is no land-and-re-grip, which is exactly what makes it worth practising.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W32 — the Leggy Flow or the b-stance flow comes back around. W33 — overhead mobility complex returns as the closer.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: bent press, all the cleans, the KB strict press. Overhead and ballistic work where the cue breaking is the ceiling.
🔥 nothing here is a lift to chase this week — see the curl note below.
**Banded shoulder prep is a KB-day anchor.** It stays even on a twenty-minute version of this session.

**⚠️ A NEW CRACKLE SHOWED UP IN THE LEFT SHOULDER on the pull-up bar last week.** The figure-8 never goes overhead, so it is the shoulder-friendly half of this session. **If the left is talking, run one round of the bent press flow and two of the figure-8.**
**The bent press is a skill, not a load.** Light bell. If the eyes leave the bell or the hip stops driving, the set is over.
**The figure-8's hike position is home base.** Every transition resets through the hike — if you lose the bell, go back to the hike before restarting rather than chasing it.
**KB curl: left arm first, and no near-failure this week.** The left bicep tendon is still irritable. Stop short of a fully straight arm, same as the gym curls.
**Optional means optional.** Missing this day entirely does not make the week incomplete.

sets.name: Warm-Up — Halos + Cossacks + Around-the-Body (Light Bell)
sets.notes:
Light bell throughout. The cossacks double as an early-warning system — how they feel tells you what kind of session this is, and that read has been more reliable than sleep quality.

**Tired-day version:** 5 reps each.

exercises.notes: Light bell. Hand-eye primer — **and the direct rehearsal for the figure-8 later**, since both are about the hand that receives the bell.
Close to the head, elbows leading. Opens the shoulders without loading them. **Go slow on the left side this week.**
**Your readiness screen.** Deep as the hips allow, heel down. Read it against your own normal — the old ankle sprain means a stiff day here is not a forecast.
Deep core before the bell gets heavy.
**Protective activation.** A bell in each hand works if no DBs are around. Straight up, squeeze, slow release.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~2 min)
sets.notes:
One round of all seven, about two minutes. Sustained tension, no rest between positions. **This is the KB-day shoulder anchor and it does not come out** — and with a new complaint on the left, this week least of all.

**Tired-day version:** 6 reps each. Exhausted: do it anyway at whatever range is smooth.

exercises.notes: Arms overhead, pull apart without letting the ribs flare.
Slow and controlled. Blades down and together.
Thumbs up, arms to a T. Traps stay quiet.
Chest height, squeeze the blades.
Rear delts. Lead with the elbows.
Diagonal pattern, full reach.
Hold the V overhead. Ribs down, shoulders packed.

sets.name: 🌀 Bent Press Flow — The Anchor
sets.notes:
**Light bell — 25-35.** Two rounds each side when fresh, one when tired.

This is the program's oldest flow and it is skill work first. **Run it as one continuous chain**, not five separate exercises: the transitions are the part worth practising. 🛑 The bent press caps the bell — if the hip stops driving or the eyes leave the bell, the flow drops a size.

**If the left shoulder is noisy, one round here is enough** and the figure-8 takes the extra.

sets.name: Strength — KB Row + Strict Press + Curl 🛑
sets.notes:
Run this between the two flows so the demanding work is not all stacked at the end.

**Tired-day version:** one round.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD: 50.** Maintenance — the real row volume lives on pull day. 50 being easy is the correct end state; do not chase it.
- Flat back, elbow past the ribs
- Slow eccentric, full stretch at the bottom

**LOAD: 50, strict — clean to rack, press straight up, no push-press.** 50 is the Arrilaga ceiling, so the pause is the progression.
- **2-3s PAUSE AT LOCKOUT every rep** — bicep by the ear, shoulder packed **DOWN**, ribs down, and hold it
- Full lockout before the count starts — no soft elbow
- **Both sides to the same standard — and if the left will not hold a quiet lockout this week, stop that side there**

**LOAD: light bell, ~25-35. LEFT ARM FIRST — match the right to it.**
- **Upper arm pinned to the ribs**, elbow does not drift forward
- **Stop short of a fully straight arm at the bottom** — the bell loads that end position harder than a dumbbell, and that is the position the left tendon dislikes
- Shoulder packed down, no shrug to start

**No near-failure sets.** The dose here is frequency for the left arm, not intensity.

sets.name: 🌀 Figure-8 → Tactical Clean — Back After Months Away
sets.notes:
**Medium bell — 25-35.** Two rounds when fresh, one when tired. **Nothing here goes overhead.**

🔆 **What the movement actually is:** the bell swings back between your legs, and the opposite hand reaches around the outside of that thigh to take it — a figure-eight traced around your legs. **The hand that catches it does not set it down and re-grip; the catch continues straight up into a clean to the rack.** Then a tactical clean brings it back down and through to the other side.

- **The pass IS the clean entry.** If you land the bell, stop, and then clean it, the skill has been skipped
- **The hike between the legs is home base** — every transition resets through it. Lose the bell, go back to the hike, restart from there
- **Tactical clean means threaded into the rack, not yanked** — no momentum hack, no forearm bang
- **Hinge, do not squat, to send the bell back.** The hips move, the knees mostly do not
- **Chest stays proud through the pass** — rounding over to reach the bell is how the low back ends up doing it

**Go light first.** Groove the pass and the clean separately for a few reps before chaining them.

sets.name: Cooldown (Hip + Shoulder Release)
sets.notes:
The figure-8's wide stance and hike position tighten the adductors and hip flexors, and one flow finished overhead. Give both ends a beat.

**Tired-day version:** 30s each.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
Passive decompression after the overhead work.
45s each side. The lunges earned this.
Adductors — the figure-8's wide stance earned this one specifically.
30s each side. QL release.

tips: Optional means optional. One round of each flow is a complete session.
The figure-8's pass IS the clean entry — no land-and-re-grip.
The hike position is home base. Lose the bell, reset through the hike.
Nothing in the figure-8 goes overhead — run more of it if the left shoulder is talking.
KB curl: left first, stop short of straight, no near-failure.
